nodes.label: TCP listen and accept contract
nodes.description: Servers open TCP, bind, listen, and accept into an empty socket. Nonblocking listeners return WouldBlock when no connection is pending; accepted sockets inherit the wrapper blocking mode.

nodes.label: Socket options and pending-connect mode constraints
nodes.description: SetNoDelay controls TCP latency policy; SetBufferSizes requests positive native-adjustable buffer sizes. Worker threads can select blocking mode, but changing blocking mode during pending connect is rejected.

nodes.label: TCP send half-close and receive EOF
nodes.description: Shutdown(Send) half-closes a TCP stream so the peer sees EOF after queued bytes while replies can still be received. The socket remains owned until Close.
nodes.norm_label: tcp send half-close and receive eof

nodes.label: Lazy shared Winsock runtime independent of windows
nodes.description: Socket and resolver operations automatically hold shared internal runtime references. Winsock starts lazily; each socket closes before releasing its reference. No window, Platform::Initialize, event pump, or main-thread service is required, and networking survives window shutdown.
nodes.norm_label: lazy shared winsock runtime independent of windows
nodes.rationale: Socket/runtime ownership must work headlessly and remain independent of window initialization or shutdown.

nodes.label: Movable owned socket lifetime
nodes.description: Socket is noncopyable and movable, closes on destruction, and closes its previous destination during move assignment. Open requires an empty socket; Close precedes reopening or retrying a failed connection. Nuclear.Platform must remain loaded until sockets are destroyed.

nodes.label: Future engine replication and session policy
nodes.description: The foundation owns native transport, address translation, readiness, diagnostics, and basic options. Peer/session identity, connection policy, message formats/framing, serialization, replication, reliability, sequencing, budgets, encryption, and authentication remain higher-level policy and are not implemented here.
nodes.norm_label: future engine replication and session policy
nodes.rationale: Separating transport from gameplay/session/wire policy keeps Nuclear.Platform an independent OS foundation and leaves replication design in higher-level engine code.

nodes.label: Headless IPv4/IPv6 UDP/TCP tests
nodes.description: The separate NetworkTests project uses ephemeral loopback ports, offline localhost/numeric resolution, and bounded waits without initializing windows. It covers both IP families, UDP empty/truncated packets, readiness/refused connections, partial TCP/half-close/EOF, move/reopen ownership, invalid input, and concurrent independent runtime lifetimes.

nodes.label: Readiness polling and bounded timeouts

nodes.label: EditorAddMenu cascading creation popup

nodes.label: EditorEntityState authoring snapshots
nodes.rationale: EditorEntityState stores authored entity values and borrowed library mesh/material references. Deleted entities restore at their original versioned ECS identity so earlier entity commands resolve. Skybox ECS/history snapshots store only the editor visibility marker, never its GPU resources. The protected editor camera is excluded from entity editing; separate EditorSceneState snapshots support scene name and preview clear-color changes. Runtime actors, audio handles and script instances are never captured. Future editable entity fields/components must extend entity snapshots.

nodes.label: EditorSceneState scene identity snapshots
nodes.rationale: EditorSceneState captures scene settings separately from entities using the borrowed active scene identity. Restore resolves the current camera instead of retaining a camera component pointer and rejects snapshots from another scene.

nodes.label: EditorSelectionRenderer
nodes.rationale: Editor-owned renderer for visible entity IDs and selection silhouettes. Owns a depth-tested R32_UINT entity-ID target, separate D32 depth, pipelines and a one-pixel staging texture. nodes.label: EditorSkybox generated cubemap ownership
nodes.rationale: EditorSkybox owns a generated blue sky, horizon and ground cubemap and requires no external texture assets. GPU creation is queued for Update. Resources are released before graphics shutdown; ECS/history snapshots retain only the visibility marker.

nodes.label: Generated skybox authoring limits

nodes.label: Gizmo history commit boundary
nodes.rationale: One released gizmo drag is one transaction independent of live update count. Canceled drags add nothing. History replay first cancels a pending viewport gesture, then restores selection, hierarchy, inspector and renderer bindings.

nodes.label: History authoring runtime boundary
nodes.rationale: Runtime-service components remain uninitialized authoring data and authoring cameras are recreated inactive without render targets. Runtime actors, audio handles and script instances are not stored by history.

nodes.label: History lifetime and exclusions
nodes.rationale: New scene, successful project creation and shutdown clear Undo and Redo. Canceling project creation preserves history. History is session-only; asset importing, filesystem operations, camera navigation, document/dock layouts and project replacement are outside scene history.

nodes.label: Interleaved scene and entity history
nodes.rationale: Scene settings share the same 128-action undo/redo order as entity edits. Scene settings replay preserves entity selection. Scene-name and clear-color edits are included in the common history alongside entity authoring transactions.

nodes.label: Editor dropdown focus and navigation
nodes.rationale: Dropdowns take keyboard focus, switch headers by hover or Left/Right, select enabled commands by Up/Down, and execute by Enter. Outside click, Escape and focus loss dismiss. Window/Manage panels opens recovery for the active document. Command capture cancellation is reconciled each frame.

nodes.norm_label: scene history keyboard and menu routing

Focused text boxes preserve uncommitted text and do not invoke scene history. Project modals block actions, focus changes reset modifiers and repeated key downs do not replay extra steps.

nodes.label: Scene history supported edits
nodes.rationale: History covers Add-menu entities/primitives, browser and asset-document mesh instantiation, deletion, committed inspector names/transforms, light properties, mesh visibility/shadow flags, kinematic flags, component addition/removal, scene names and preview clear color. Skybox creation, visibility, deletion and restoration also use entity history. Scene and entity transactions share one bounded undo/redo order; scene settings replay preserves entity selection.

nodes.label: Skybox entity history and reset
nodes.rationale: Skybox creation, visibility, deletion and restoration participate in normal entity undo/redo. Hiding or removing the sky restores the scene clear color. New scenes start without a skybox. Repeated Add selects the existing background instead of creating a second one.

nodes.label: Queued GPU pick readback
nodes.rationale: Clicks queue a fresh entity-ID render and one-pixel staging readback for Update, avoiding GPU work inside input dispatch. Resize, mode and modal changes can invalidate a queued click. ID values map to live versioned ECS identities.

nodes.label: Selection outline occlusion

nodes.label: Selection resource lifetime

nodes.label: Viewport mesh selection

nodes.label: Yellow selection silhouette

nodes.label: Native dock transfers and recovery
nodes.rationale: Tools dock only within their owner document, with drop previews, collapsed empty groups and splitters. A browser document moves its complete layout when detached/redocked. Native close returns contents to their owning groups. Window recovery and Reset layout affect only the active document; they preserve other layouts/windows. Layout history is session-only.

nodes.label: Text quality validation 2026-11-08
nodes.rationale: Debug x64 editor, editor-test, UI-test and Windows platform-test builds passed. Complete D3D11 editor checks passed at 1440x900 and 960x600 with wrapping actions, small-panel imports and synthetic 125% detached redocking. Headless UI and both 60-frame D3D11 modes passed a fractional-contour readback rejecting a two-pixel halo. Platform DPI queries and suggested bounds passed; embedded manifest was inspected and main/detached readbacks visually reviewed. Physical mixed-DPI monitor movement, other graphics backends and Release were not checked.

nodes.label: Window::GetDpiScale
nodes.rationale: Returns pixels per 96-DPI logical unit, or 1 for an empty window. Actual monitor DPI requires host executable awareness; the foundation does not alter process-wide awareness for other applications.

nodes.label: WM_DPICHANGED
nodes.rationale: Applies OS-suggested physical window bounds and emits WindowResize even if pixel dimensions stay unchanged, allowing clients to refresh scale and swap-chain dimensions.

nodes.label: Explicit focus for retained overlays
nodes.rationale: UIContext.SetFocus selects an attached visible enabled focusable widget by stable ID; zero/invalid IDs clear focus. It cancels the previous control and reveals scroll ancestors through the same path as pointer/Tab navigation. Editor menus use it for immediate keyboard ownership; all calls use the UI/event thread.

nodes.label: Fractional scale redocking
nodes.rationale: Tab drags convert source logical coordinates to physical desktop coordinates and destination physical client coordinates to destination logical coordinates using each context's scale. A detached redock at synthetic 125% passed.

nodes.label: Monitor DPI text scaling
nodes.rationale: The editor and focused test executable embed PerMonitorV2 awareness. Main and detached UI contexts use their own window's GetDpiScale, preserving monitor text size when windows shrink. The platform applies OS-suggested bounds on DPI changes.

nodes.label: Executable DPI awareness
nodes.rationale: The host executable owns its awareness declaration. The editor embeds PerMonitorV2; the foundation does not change process-wide awareness for other hosts.

nodes.label: Editor monitor DPI policy
nodes.rationale: UIContext remains explicitly scaled. The editor supplies Window::GetDpiScale for main and detached contexts and declares per-monitor executable awareness; other clients retain their own scaling policies.

nodes.label: Single pixel SDF antialiasing
nodes.rationale: The retained text shader samples a single-channel SDF atlas and uses half of fwidth on each side of the contour for a one-pixel antialiasing band, keeping small letter edges sharper.

nodes.rationale: Imported fonts preserve fractional advances, bounds, atlas UVs, ascender/line metrics and kerning. Height is clamped to 8..256 pixels/em and initial repertoire is ASCII. nodes.rationale: UIRenderer.Render optionally accepts a borrowed render target matching its initialized main swap-chain color format. Null retains main-buffer rendering. nodes.label: Independent retained UI module lifecycle
nodes.rationale: AutoInitUIModule defaults true when Graphics is automatic. UI depends on Graphics and Assets without making Assets depend on UI. Renderer/default font follow assets; roots clear before borrowed assets, and GPU resources release before Graphics. EnableImGui is independent.

nodes.label: Painter-ordered GPU quads
nodes.rationale: CPU quads preserve painter order and effective clipping. Dynamic buffers batch only adjacent matching textures/scissors, preserving alpha order. Drawing occurs on the swap-chain target after scene rendering without clearing, before optional ImGui and presentation.

nodes.label: Allocation accounting bounds and rejection
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: At most 65536 live identities, 256 categories, and 128 characters per category. Null/zero-sized, duplicate, overflowing, and over-capacity registrations are rejected; rejection counts disclose incomplete coverage. Unknown/double frees return false.

nodes.label: ProfilingModule dependency and shutdown lifecycle
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: AutoInitProfilingModule defaults true. Register after Graphics when enabled and release GPU queries before graphics teardown; CPU-only initialization is supported.

nodes.label: Unambiguous renderer match or explicit LUID selection
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Automatic adapter selection is withheld if multiple GPUs share renderer PCI IDs. Select an exact LUID in the UI or SetGpuMemoryAdapter; selected memory and rendering adapters may intentionally differ, and UI names the selected adapter.
nodes.norm_label: unambiguous renderer match or explicit luid selection
nodes.source_location: Enabling capture and opening the profiler

nodes.label: CPU and GPU frame capture boundaries
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Capture starts after events before queued work/module updates and includes client Update/Render scopes. GPU queries end before Present; CPU frame time ends after Present and includes presentation blocking. Direct BeginFrame/EndFrame share boundaries; earlier work is excluded.
nodes.norm_label: cpu and gpu frame capture boundaries
nodes.source_location: Enabling capture and opening the profiler

nodes.label: Normal submission required for GPU completion
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: D3D11 timestamp results require that frame FinishFrame. Engine Present supplies normal lifecycle; custom loops must honor Diligent context completion rather than forcing profiler waits.
nodes.norm_label: normal submission required for gpu completion
nodes.rationale: A profiler must observe normal frame completion asynchronously rather than force GPU synchronization and distort the timing being measured.

nodes.label: Headless Debug CPU and accounting validation
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Debug CPU tests verified topology/memory queries, interval validity, concurrent explicit accounting, CPU scopes/aggregation, cross-frame rejection, and history/capture limits without a window.
nodes.norm_label: headless debug cpu and accounting validation

nodes.label: Disable and reset preserve live allocation identities
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Disabling blocks new tracking while permitting existing frees. ResetCounters keeps live allocations while resetting peaks and cumulative counters. Tracked bytes remain separate from OS working set/private commit and do not attribute GPU allocations.
nodes.norm_label: disable and reset preserve live allocation identities

nodes.label: Independent durations and native query overlap limits
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Duration uses independent timestamp pairs and allows overlapping regions. Same-type native pipeline-statistics/occlusion queries cannot overlap on a context. Disable module capture for custom overlapping pipeline queries because capture occupies one. OpenGL only supplies clipping invocations for pipeline statistics.
nodes.norm_label: independent durations and native query overlap limits

nodes.label: Opt-in frame capture
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: EnableProfiling defaults false. Enable through startup description, ProfilingModule::SetEnabled, or the profiler Capture checkbox. Registration alone does not record frames.
nodes.source_location: Enabling capture and opening the profiler

nodes.label: Exact session-local GPU adapter identity
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: EnumerateGpus returns names, PCI vendor/device IDs, opaque session-local adapter LUIDs, software flags, and capacities.
nodes.source_location: Platform CPU, GPU, and memory queries

nodes.label: Asynchronous GPU frame correlation and validity
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: GPU results update their original frame IDs asynchronously. Pending, unsupported, disjoint, invalid, or dropped results never become valid zero durations. Drop/error counters and support/validity flags are exposed.
nodes.norm_label: asynchronous gpu frame correlation and validity
nodes.source_location: Enabling capture and opening the profiler

nodes.label: Bounded owned frame snapshots
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: GetSnapshot returns a mutex-consistent owned copy; history retains at most 240 completed frames and 2048 CPU scope records per frame.
nodes.source_location: Enabling capture and opening the profiler

nodes.label: Monotonic nanosecond clock
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: GetTimestampNanoseconds measures elapsed monotonic nanoseconds, not CPU cycles or calendar time.
nodes.source_location: Platform CPU, GPU, and memory queries

nodes.label: Duration, Timestamp, Occlusion, PipelineStatistics
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: GpuQuery provides paired-timestamp Duration, single Timestamp, sample-count Occlusion, and backend-dependent PipelineStatistics. Duration results are milliseconds; timestamps include raw ticks and frequency.

nodes.label: Optional Diligent backend query features
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Graphics requests timestamp, pipeline-statistics, and occlusion support optionally on D3D11/D3D12/OpenGL/Vulkan. Unsupported queries do not fail startup; runtime profiling validation currently covers D3D11 only.

nodes.label: Fixed bounded asynchronous GPU query pools
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Initialize with a live retained Diligent device and 1..256 submissions, default 8. A full pool returns CapacityExceeded; polling later frames does not flush, spin, wait for idle, grow pending pools, or overwrite in-flight results.
nodes.norm_label: fixed bounded asynchronous gpu query pools

nodes.label: Profiling validation and hardware coverage limits

nodes.label: Periodic counters and normalized CPU load
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: OS process/system and selected-GPU memory counters are sampled at most every 500 ms during capture. CPU utilization requires two samples; process load is normalized to all logical processors on a 0..100 percent scale.
nodes.norm_label: periodic counters and normalized cpu load
nodes.source_location: Enabling capture and opening the profiler

nodes.label: Inclusive per-thread CPU scopes
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: PROFILE_CPU uses mutex-protected CpuScope recording, copies up to 128 label characters into fixed entry storage, and supports worker threads. Inclusive nested totals overlap; worker wall-time totals may exceed frame wall time.

nodes.label: Legacy monotonic CPU timer in milliseconds
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling

nodes.norm_label: legacy monotonic cpu timer in milliseconds

nodes.label: Legacy GPU helper result and shutdown contract
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Profiler_GPU/PROFILE_GPU use bounded queries. End(double&) fixes by-value output and writes completed seconds while preserving pending output. End() returns ambiguous zero while pending, so prefer explicit GpuQueryStatus. Static helpers require Shutdown before renderer teardown.
nodes.norm_label: legacy gpu helper result and shutdown contract

nodes.label: Cumulative CPU counter units and intervals

nodes.norm_label: cumulative cpu counter units and intervals

nodes.label: Per-process exact-LUID GPU memory budgets
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling

nodes.source_location: Platform CPU, GPU, and memory queries

nodes.label: Physical and process memory semantics

nodes.source_location: Platform CPU, GPU, and memory queries

nodes.label: Diagnostic result and output preservation
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling

nodes.source_location: Platform CPU, GPU, and memory queries

nodes.label: CPU scope frame lifetime and drops
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: Scopes must finish or join before their original frame ends. Cross-frame and over-capacity records are dropped rather than assigned to another frame. Capture/history storage still allocates memory.
nodes.norm_label: cpu scope frame lifetime and drops
nodes.rationale: Keep each inclusive CPU region attached to its actual originating frame; late records must not contaminate another frame.

nodes.label: System CPU multi-group limitation
nodes.community_name: CPU, GPU, memory, and performance profiling
nodes.description: System CPU counters are unavailable on machines with multiple processor groups because Windows GetSystemTimes only covers one group; process counters remain usable.
nodes.rationale: Do not present GetSystemTimes for a single processor group as a whole-machine CPU load measurement.
nodes.source_location: Platform CPU, GPU, and memory queries

nodes.description: Thread-safe MemoryProfiler starts enabled and accounts only caller-registered pointers, sizes, and categories. TrackFree records before actual free/reuse; ownership remains with the allocator. No global new/delete interception, vendor coverage, call stacks, or real deallocation.

nodes.label: Audio backend plugin ABI
nodes.description: Audio plugin ABI checks size, version, name, and factories. Shutdown destroys the backend before unloading its DLL; JSON manifests are metadata and are not scanned.

nodes.label: Audio backend DLL selection
nodes.description: AudioModule selects XAudio2 or OpenAL by backend DLL name. AudioSystem connects sources/listeners; the descriptor can override the executable plugin directory.

nodes.label: Client application callbacks
nodes.description: Client supplies empty default callbacks. LoadClient calls Initialize and Load before the blocking loop; clients choose how to update scene systems.

nodes.label: EngineModule lifecycle contract
nodes.description: EngineModule is the shared lifecycle base for built-in/application modules. CallbackModule currently adapts only AssetManager.

nodes.label: Asset readiness states
nodes.description: IAsset exposes Unknown, Deserialized, Queued, Loaded, and Created states. A returned non-null asset may still have asynchronous work pending and need not have ready GPU resources.

nodes.label: IScriptingBackend opaque interface
nodes.description: IScriptingBackend plus opaque class/object wrappers keep native script assets and components independent of Nuclear.Managed.

nodes.label: NativeCalls Cdecl ABI
nodes.description: InitBindings uploads native callbacks into Nuclear.NativeCalls unmanaged Cdecl function-pointer fields. NativeString handles strings and booleans cross as 32-bit integers.

nodes.label: Scripting source map
nodes.description: Maps generic scripting interfaces, C# backend hosting/registration/bindings, included bridge discovery, script object lifecycle, and managed API examples.

nodes.label: Retained editor consumes runtime scene
nodes.description: Nuclear.Editor uses Nuclear::UI and the shared ECS scene. Its client disables ImGui, audio, physics, scripts and workers; an editor-owned RenderSystem renders to a camera texture sampled by a retained widget. Gameplay systems are not driven.

nodes.label: ModuleManager lifecycle orchestration
nodes.description: One EngineModule lifecycle base supports owned, borrowed singleton, and DLL modules. Dependency validation rejects missing names/cycles; failure and shutdown reverse completed phases.

nodes.label: GraphicsModule Diligent integration
nodes.description: Owns Diligent device/context/swap-chain integration and graphics resource creation.

nodes.label: Independent networking transport layer
nodes.description: Portable endpoints and movable sockets expose Windows nonblocking UDP/TCP, readiness, resolution, and shared Winsock lifetime independently of windows. Startup registers no replication module or wire protocol; future replication/session/serialization policy belongs in the engine.

nodes.label: RenderSystem ECS renderer
nodes.description: RenderSystem connects ECS cameras, meshes, lights, shader registration/baking, paths, and passes, iterating active cameras and constructing FrameRenderData.

nodes.label: RenderingModule shared resources
nodes.description: RenderingModule supplies shared camera/animation constant buffers and final render targets.

nodes.label: C++/HLSL resource-name contract
nodes.description: Resource names such as NEMat_Diffuse1 and NEStatic_Camera connect shaders to C++ binding logic; CPU buffer layouts and shader reflection must remain aligned.

nodes.label: Scene and EnTT registry
nodes.description: Scene owns the EnTT registry, system manager, main-camera pointer, and current scene-asset pointer.

nodes.label: EntityInfoComponent transform/name
nodes.description: Scene::CreateEntity adds EntityInfoComponent carrying the transform and name; dependent components should use that creation path.

nodes.label: ScriptingModule backend registry
nodes.description: ScriptingModule owns a registry and selects one backend; Engine::Start registers C# before scripting initialization. Lua remains an unregistered scaffold.

nodes.label: Managed component registration
nodes.description: ScriptingRegistry maps Nuclear.Managed type IDs to implemented EntityInfo and Light component add/has operations; unknown IDs fail without inserting empty callbacks.

nodes.label: Managed entity script callbacks
nodes.description: ScriptingSystem binds entities before OnStart and invokes OnUpdate. Backend object handles are destroyed before context unload, and class lifetime tokens reject stale construction.

nodes.label: NuclearShader TOML descriptions
nodes.description: ShaderParser reads TOML-style NuclearShader descriptions accepting HLSL paths or embedded source.

nodes.label: ShaderPipeline variants and reflection
nodes.description: ShaderPipeline and its variant factory bake pipeline variants and reflection/bindings; mesh/material state selects variants and resources.

nodes.label: SystemManager unordered updates
nodes.description: SystemManager stores shared systems in an unordered_map. Update_All does not guarantee insertion-order simulation, and clients drive their scene systems explicitly.

nodes.label: System update order unspecified
nodes.description: SystemManager uses unordered-map iteration; adding systems in a sequence does not guarantee that update order.

nodes.label: TextureCreateTask main-thread GPU creation
nodes.description: TextureCreateTask creates graphics resources on the main thread, removes queue membership, and cleans temporary image data. Task implementations may self-delete in OnEnd.

nodes.label: TextureImportTask worker decode
nodes.description: TextureImportTask decodes source data, can export NEMeta, and queues TextureCreateTask for main-thread resource creation.

nodes.label: C# static scripting backend
nodes.description: The C# backend is a static library linked into Nuclear.Engine; its manifest is metadata rather than dynamic backend discovery.

nodes.label: Nuclear.Managed .NET bridge
nodes.description: The included Coral-derived Nuclear.Managed fork hosts .NET 10, selecting a stable hostfxr and loading ScriptCore plus client assemblies in one collectible context; CoreCLR remains process-wide.

nodes.label: ThreadingModule worker/main-thread queues
nodes.description: ThreadingModule manages a worker pool and a separate main-thread task list; the enabled engine loop executes up to one queued main-thread task per frame.

nodes.label: External engine module DLL ABI
nodes.description: Versioned GetNuclearEngineModulePlugin factories contribute named modules and dependencies. Startup scanning loads sorted Nuclear.Module.*.dll files; destroy callbacks precede unload and hot reload is unsupported.

nodes.label: Audio playback unvalidated by build
nodes.description: XAudio2/OpenAL plugins load by name without manifest discovery or hot swapping. A build does not verify audio-device initialization or playback.

nodes.label: Retained runtime UI
nodes.rationale: UIModule registers after Graphics and Assets. UIContext owns roots, layout, focus and capture separately from ECS entities. Portable input precedes gameplay callbacks and drawing follows client rendering but precedes optional ImGui/presentation.

nodes.label: Focused WASD camera navigation
nodes.rationale: Click the viewport then hold W/A/S/D for camera-relative forward/left/back/right flight. Elapsed frame time and camera speed determine movement; diagonals are normalized. Key release, Escape and viewport/window focus loss stop motion. Right-look can run alongside flight; transform drags pause it. Inspector typing and modals are isolated.

nodes.label: Camera navigation during transform editing
nodes.rationale: Right drag looks, wheel dollies and focused WASD flies. Camera movement is paused during transform drags. Input in inspector fields or project modals does not navigate.

nodes.label: TransformGizmo drag snapshot ownership
nodes.rationale: TransformGizmo owns drag math and original position/quaternion/scale, never an ECS target pointer. GameViewPort resolves the live selected ECS handle on every event.

nodes.label: World-axis single-selection gizmo limits
nodes.rationale: One selected entity is edited in world axes. Snapping and local-axis mode remain unimplemented. Select mode now picks visible mesh surfaces in the viewport, while completed transform drags continue to participate in scene undo/redo history.

nodes.label: Gizmo projection and drag geometry
nodes.rationale: Projection uses actual CameraComponent.mCameraData.View, since the current GetViewMatrix accessor returns Model. Move axes solve closest ray/axis points; free move and rotation intersect ray/plane. Edge-on rings use a screen-tangent fallback.

nodes.label: Deterministic and D3D11 gizmo validation

Tests cover XYZ move/rotate/scale, free move, uniform/mirrored scaling, edge-on rotation, zero quaternion, hidden pivots, scaled input, Escape/focus/Tab/resize rollback and deleted targets. D3D11 tests drag while inspector rebuilds, commit on outside release, right-drag camera and render all modes. Physical mouse feel, Release and other backends are unvalidated.

nodes.label: Import picker ownership and dispatch
nodes.rationale: The focused main or detached editor window owns the picker. Opening and selection run from Update outside retained input dispatch, and file selection preserves the process working directory.

nodes.label: Modal project input isolation
nodes.rationale: Disabling workspace restricts pointer and Tab input to Create/Cancel modal until removal. Callback requests are rebuilt from Update while the shell persists.

nodes.label: Native asset import picker
nodes.rationale: Import... opens a native single-file picker from every browser category, initially at the browsing directory. The supported-assets filter covers textures, geometry, NuclearShader and TTF; All files permits unsupported selections that receive existing format feedback. Cancellation creates no asset.

nodes.label: WASD and Select validation
nodes.rationale: Debug editor and focused tests passed after adding WASD and Select. Checks cover four directions, releases, frame subdivision, diagonal speed, opposing keys, focus and window cancellation, inspector input, right-look, transform-drag suspension, hidden/inactive handles and drag rollback. D3D11 readbacks cover Select and both workspace sizes. Physical input feel, Release and other backends remain unverified.

nodes.label: Offscreen scene camera surface
nodes.rationale: GameViewPort samples the camera color target through retained UI. Right-drag looks, wheel moves forward/backward and Frame Selected places the camera six world units behind selection along view direction. Select-mode left-click queues depth-tested visible-mesh picking; background clears selection. Capture ends on release/cancel, and viewport keyboard focus is retained by selection.

nodes.label: Scene-target format and GPU viewport contract
nodes.norm_label: scene-target format and gpu viewport contract
nodes.rationale: Camera RGBA8 sRGB target matches PSO and uses separate depth. Rendering sets physical scene-surface viewport, restores swap-chain target and lets engine draw UI/present. Resize updates camera targets/projection without UI renderer rebake.

nodes.label: Queued imports and explicit GPU readiness
nodes.norm_label: queued imports and explicit gpu readiness
nodes.rationale: Explicit Import actions queue Update work. Existing importers load textures, geometry, shaders and TTF; model materials/animations are omitted and scene meshes use default material. Synchronous decoding still queues GPU mesh tasks, drained on the main thread. Readiness is separate; failed textures do not report fallback success. Picker selection reuses the existing load-only project-session import flow; there is no source-file copying or disk project persistence.

nodes.label: Editor uses retained UI throughout
nodes.rationale: Startup sets EnableImGui=false; editor sources do not include/call ImGui. Old dialog and imgui.ini are removed. Engine legacy sample/debug ImGui remains separately optional.

nodes.label: Scaled and scrollable workspace
nodes.rationale: The workspace keeps monitor-scaled text at smaller window sizes rather than fitting a 1440x900 design. Draggable splitters control dock proportions and empty groups collapse. Viewport actions wrap at narrow widths; bottom tools keep at least 180 logical units capped at 60% of workspace height. Hierarchy, properties, assets and diagnostics retain scroll views and widget state across docking.

nodes.label: Session-only editor feature limits
nodes.rationale: Projects, scenes, scene undo/redo history, tab history and dock layouts are held in memory. Document tabs, docking, native windows and up to 128 scene authoring undo/redo actions are implemented. Disk project/layout persistence, play mode and shader/material authoring remain absent.

nodes.label: Session-only asset import
nodes.rationale: Selected resources use existing load-only importers and belong to the current project session. No source copying or disk project persistence is added.

nodes.rationale: Select, Move, Rotate and Scale share the toolbar above the scene viewport with Frame selected and Delete selected. EditorToolbar wraps the actions into additional rows at narrow widths while preserving text size. Q/G/E/R choose tools only while the viewport has keyboard focus.

nodes.label: World-axis Move Rotate Scale gizmos
nodes.rationale: Selected entities expose red X, green Y, blue Z arrows/rings/endpoint boxes. Select/Move/Rotate/Scale buttons share the bar above the viewport with Frame selected and Delete selected. Focused Q/G/E/R choose those tools; inspector typing does not.

nodes.label: Editor transform gizmo source map
nodes.rationale: TransformGizmo.h/.cpp own world-axis handle math and drawing; GameViewPort owns pointer capture and rollback. Editor.md documents operation and controls.

nodes.label: Retained screen-space widgets
nodes.rationale: Nuclear::UI is a retained widget tree rendered directly through Diligent without ImGui types, atlas, drawing or input state. The editor uses it throughout; legacy sample/debug ImGui is optional.

nodes.label: Selector scaling and integration checks

Separate SelectorTests covers settings, expanded focus, resize, native launch, clear-history, import cancellation and selector/UI round trips. 2026-11-07 D3D11 checks passed with ImGui disabled/enabled and reviewed readbacks. Other sample content/imports are outside the check.

nodes.norm_label: session model and retained controller ownership
nodes.rationale: NuclearEditor owns Project and EditorUI. UIContext owns the shell; Nuclear.Editor.h remains an include-only compatibility facade. Implementations are class files explicitly registered by native projects.

nodes.label: Workspace ownership and modal isolation
nodes.rationale: The outer browser dock area owns complete document layouts, each owning its own dock groups and splitters. Tool metadata records an immutable owner document. TabStrip owns only headers and gestures. Transfers queue for Update through TakeChild and retain identities. Floating documents carry their complete custom layout; window-origin bindings update after transfer. Modals isolate all windows and teardown validates IDs before clearing callbacks.

nodes.label: Exclusive widget-tree ownership
nodes.rationale: UIContext owns roots by unique_ptr and panels exclusively own children. Returned widget/parent/context references are borrowed until removal. Stable nonzero WidgetId resolves through Find; removed IDs return null. Widgets are not ECS entities or scene snapshot data.

nodes.label: Retained widget ownership transfer
nodes.rationale: PanelWidget.TakeChild transfers an immediate child outside input/deferred dispatch, cancels focus/capture before detach, unregisters parent/context and retains identity/content. Missing IDs return null; unsafe dispatch transfers throw logic_error. Queue transfers for client Update and use IsDispatching to inspect the guard.

nodes.label: Portable event routing and bubbling
nodes.rationale: The engine routes platform input before gameplay mouse callbacks. Mouse pixel positions are scaled to logical coordinates; Windows button events carry positions. Frontmost enabled interactive widgets receive input and unhandled replies bubble over stable ID snapshots. Labels/images do not block underlying controls.

nodes.label: Engine compatibility
nodes.description: Forwarding engine Window/Input headers require platform include/lib/project reference and shipping DLL. SDL accessor removed; native handles used only at boundaries.

nodes.label: Nuclear.Platform
nodes.description: Independent C++20 DLL replaces SDL and owns native windows/events/input/cursors/clipboard/executable lookup/library loading; public API uses standard types and opaque handles.

nodes.label: Input focus lifecycle
nodes.description: Keys/buttons clear on focus loss. Locked foreground raw-relative cursor hides/confines; confinement suspends on focus loss and restores on gain.

nodes.label: Plugin policy boundary
nodes.description: Module/audio discovery, ABI validation, ownership and teardown remain engine policy; native library operations go through foundation.

nodes.label: Borrowed native lifetimes
nodes.description: Native handles, event-window pointers and library symbol addresses cannot outlive owners. Destroy purges queued events, repeat cleanup is safe and live windows prevent unregister.

nodes.label: Networking
nodes.description: Nonblocking UDP/TCP endpoints, DNS/readiness and automatic shared Winsock lifetime work without windows/event-thread startup.

nodes.label: Platform::Window
nodes.description: Noncopyable window; client-pixel dimensions and UTF-8 title, fullscreen is primary-monitor borderless without display-mode change.

nodes.label: Windows x64
nodes.description: Only implemented native backend; standard headers do not establish complete engine portability.

nodes.label: Platform::PollEvent
nodes.description: Pumps Windows messages into portable queued events before each frame; physical keys preserve USB HID IDs shared with C#.

nodes.label: Platform::FileSystem
nodes.description: Remains engine-owned because it depends on Core::Path, DataBlob, logging and shader processing.
nodes.rationale: It is not a dependency-free native platform file service.

nodes.label: Platform::Initialize
nodes.description: Runs on the thread that will create windows and poll events.

nodes.label: Engine smoke test
nodes.description: Separate 12-frame D3D11/ImGui test resizes 960x540, receives mouse/scroll and shuts down without audio/physics/scripting/threads.

nodes.label: Windows smoke tests
nodes.description: Separate platform project validates synthetic key/Unicode/wheel/window/library/lifetime behavior; does not prove physical devices/camera/audio.

nodes.label: Unicode input
nodes.description: Text input is distinct from physical keys; Windows combines UTF-16 surrogate pairs to scalar TextInput events.

nodes.label: ImGuiPlatform
nodes.description: Translates events, clipboard, cursor, dimensions/timing into ImGui while preserving Diligent rendering/main-window docking. No secondary native viewports, gamepads or explicit IME composition placement.

nodes.label: DPI adjusted window sizing
nodes.rationale: Native framed-window sizing uses DPI-adjusted nonclient extents so requested client dimensions remain physical pixels.

nodes.label: Reserved path aliases
nodes.description: Core::Path expands reserved aliases. Engine startup sets Assets, NuclearAssets, and CurrentPath; clients add CommonAssets/EditorAssets. Relative paths depend on the working directory.

nodes.label: Asset document GPU readiness
nodes.rationale: Texture previews require Created state and a real texture view. Synchronous texture import preserves Created from successful GPU upload. Created mesh counts use vertex buffer sizes and retained index counts after decoded arrays are released. Assets remain library-owned.
